title: Workshop on GitHub
description: The Workshop on GitHub was designed to introduce students to one of the most essential platforms used in the software industry today. The session began with an overview of version control and why it is critical for modern software development and team collaboration.Nearly 50 Participants learned how to create and manage repositories, understand commits, branches, and pull requests, and work effectively in collaborative environments. The workshop emphasized practical exposure, allowing students to explore GitHub’s interface and real-world workflows. Special focus was given to open-source contributions and how GitHub can be used to build a strong technical portfolio. The speakers also guided students on maintaining clean project structures and proper documentation practices. By the end of the workshop, participants had a clearer understanding of how GitHub supports innovation, teamwork, and professional growth in the tech ecosystem.

title: Seminar with IBM Team
description: The Webinar with the IBM Team was a highly insightful session that connected students directly with professionals from a global technology leader. The webinar focused on current industry trends, emerging technologies, and how large organizations like IBM innovate and solve real-world problems. The speakers shared valuable insights into domains such as cloud computing, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, and enterprise solutions. Students were introduced to real industry workflows, team cultures, and the skills required to thrive in a corporate technology environment. The session also highlighted career opportunities at IBM, including internships, certifications, and early-career programs. A dedicated interaction segment allowed participants to ask questions about career growth, project development, and industry readiness. Overall, the webinar motivated students to align their academic learning with practical industry demands and future opportunities.

title: Programming Logic And Career Pathways
description: The Workshop on Programming Logic and Career Pathways aimed to strengthen students’ foundations in logical thinking and problem-solving, which are crucial for any programming discipline. The session covered core concepts such as algorithmic thinking, breaking down problems, and designing efficient logical flows before writing code. Through examples and interactive discussions, students were encouraged to think like developers rather than just language learners. Alongside technical logic, the workshop explored various career pathways available in the technology sector, including software development, data science, cybersecurity, AI, and product-based roles. The speakers discussed industry expectations, essential skills, and how students can strategically prepare themselves from college onwards. Guidance was also provided on internships, project-building, and continuous learning. This event helped nearly 80 students gain both technical clarity and career direction.
